newsitem.title: UK: Med oil products mostly steady despite firm Brent.
newsitem.headline: Med oil products mostly steady despite firm Brent.

text.p: Mediterranean oil products were mostly steady on Wednesday, traders said.
Gasoline was little changed as NYMEX failed to move far but the situation remains very tight in the prompt period and demand is expected to emerge for early March.
"I do not see any cargoes left for February," a dealer said.
Naphtha was weaker by up to $3 despite stronger crude, on the back of an Italian 25,000 tonne 71 paraffinic cargo sold at $216 cif Antwerp. The cargo was to arrive by the end of Feb.
Traders said naphtha had been due a correction, but should regain some strength in early March.
Gas oil was a touch busier with a Saras 0.2 25,000 tonne cargo trading at high fob quotes +$2.75 loading March 6-8.
Russian material was understood to be bid at cif high quotes -50 cents, pretty much unchanged from the high cif quotes flat to 50 cents heard yesterday.
A Skikda cargo loading Feb 20-22 was available and could probably be secured for a price close to that of Russian.
High sulphur fuel oil remained in the doldrums.
Prices for low sulphur cargoes were unchanged and buying interest was still as bad as ever. A trader fixed an 80,000 tonne cargo to load around now and sail from Sarroch to Cuba.
Dealers said this was high sulphur fuel oil.
